draft.title: Motivating employees
card: Motivation is the drive that makes staff want to do their work well. Motivated staff tend to try harder and are more likely to stay.
rewards that give staff money, such as pay rises, bonuses and commission on sales.
rewards that do not pay money, such as praise, flexible hours, a good workplace and chances to learn and move up.
Money can matter, but it is not the only thing that motivates people. Many businesses use a mix of both kinds.
draft.remember: Staff can be motivated with money or without it, and a mix often suits.

a.q: A gym in Cairns gives its trainers a bonus for each new member they sign up. What kind of motivation is this?
opts: Financial, because it pays trainers extra money
Non-financial, because it rewards good effort
Financial, because it gives trainers more time off
Non-financial, because it gives trainers recognition
a.why: A bonus is extra money, so it is a financial reward. It rewards effort, but that does not make it non-financial, because what matters is whether the reward is money.
a.clue: Look at what the trainers receive.

b.q: Sam's café in Bendigo cannot afford to raise wages. Which step would still be a way to motivate staff?
opts: Let staff choose some of their own shifts
Cut the bonus that staff were promised
Pay a commission on every coffee sold
Offer a pay rise to the best barista
b.why: Letting staff choose shifts is flexible hours, a non-financial reward that costs little. Commission and a pay rise are financial and need extra money, and cutting a bonus would lower motivation.
b.clue: The café cannot spend more on pay.

a.best: Financial, because it pays trainers extra money

b.best: Let staff choose some of their own shifts
